paper.title_en: Optical trapping of neutral atoms via magnetic-dipole transitions
paper.abstract_en: Optical trapping of neutral atoms is almost universally described as an electric-dipole (E1) effect. We show that the magnetic field of light, acting on a magnetic-dipole (M1) transition, can induce an ac Zeeman shift significantly larger than the ac Stark shift, thereby enabling magnetic trapping. We construct the M1 polarizability tensor and identify a critical detuning $δ_c$, independent of optical power, below which the magnetic interaction dominates. We analyze suitable trapping parameters and possible loss mechanisms, particularly for the intraconfigurational transitions $^3H_6\rightarrow{}^3H_5$ of erbium at $1437.13$~nm and $^5I_8\rightarrow{}^5I_7$ of dysprosium at $2418.84$~nm. We propose two trapping configurations: a hybrid magnetic/electric optical tweezer and an optical lattice with separated magnetic and electric antinodes, producing state-dependent purely magnetic and purely electric trapping wells. Our results present optical magnetic fields as a suitable resource to expand the toolbox for atomic manipulation.
